Retry thread traversal if it fails

- Build successful

snapshot.c
- (init_snapshot_store)
Change the ability to retry thread traversal.

Prior to this change if NtQuerySystemInformation() failed then this
program would exit unless the force option was used, in which case it
would retry thread traversal every second.

Now if thread traversal fails due to NtQuerySystemInformation() then
this function will by default retry traversal as many times as it can
up to a full second. If a succesful traversal could not be completed by
that time then the program will exit unless the force option is used,
in which case it will retry almost all different types of failed thread
traversals due to NtQuerySystemInformation() indefinitely with no wait.

usage.c
- (print_more_options_and_exit)
Update the force option's usage to show the changed behavior used when
NtQuerySystemInformation() fails.

Reread the handle list if an entry is bad

- Build successful

desktop_hook.c
- (init_desktop_hook_store)
Add the ability to retry when reading the HANDLEENTRYs.

Prior to this change if two or more handles contained the same HOOK
kernel address (pHead) then this program would exit:

..\desktop_hook.c line 651, init_desktop_hook_store(): Duplicate pHead.

And that is usually because rarely it can occur that a HOOK address is
reused at exactly the moment that this program reads the handle table.
To remedy that this function will now retry reading the handle list for
a full second before exiting, or indefinitely if the force option is
used. For more information review the source comments.

usage.c
- (print_more_options_and_exit)
Update the force option's usage to show that it will also retry reading
the HANDLEENTRY list indefinitely.

Fix hook ignore bug

Fix a bug introduced with the hook->ignore feature that caused
inaccurate monitoring if any filtering option was enabled.
Introduced on
1d2d6d7443e5bd59fe5130a007a7a6a3306b4fb2 10-06-2011

- Build Successful

desktop_hook.c
- (is_hook_wanted) Remove the hook->ignore check:
init_desktop_hook_store() sets hook->ignore by using the return value
of is_hook_wanted( hook ). is_hook_wanted() checks hook->ignore to
determine whether the hook was ignored. It is checking hook->ignore
before it is actually set, and if hook->ignore is nonzero then it will
remain so. Basically the ignore value ends up incorrectly being from
another hook from a previous snapshot since the memory is reused.
